purpose: Teach: アンプ/エンタープライズ/タイムズ/バーツ/カンパニー/キーパー/エコノミスト/ウィルコム

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、現場のアンプ、つまり音響機器も鑑識されますね
lines.en: The police do have the audio equipment at the scene forensically analyzed, don't they?
lines.style: Measured, slightly deferential. Respectful pause before the assumption. Nodding along with Kenji's own logic. Calm, even breath.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、エンタープライズ向けセキュリティの研修もされますね
lines.en: And the police do provide security training for enterprise-level organizations, right?
lines.style: Continuing the thread with steady interest. Slightly higher inflection at the end—genuine question, not just confirmation. Still cooperative in tone.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、海外タイムズ系紙の犯罪報道も把握されますね
lines.en: The police also monitor international news coverage of crimes—from outlets like the Times, for example.
lines.style: Same measured tempo. Matter-of-fact statement disguised as a question. A beat of thought before the example. Still building the list calmly.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、海外通貨、つまりバーツ等の偽造捜査もされますね
lines.en: They investigate counterfeiting of foreign currency too—baht and so on.
lines.style: Slight shift to more factual ground. Less inflection at the end. Acknowledging complexity without hesitation. Breath steady and deliberate.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、海外カンパニーが関わる事件も担当されますね
lines.en: And they handle cases involving foreign companies as well.
lines.style: Quick, efficient. The rhythm accelerates slightly—moving down the list. Still cooperative but with less space between thoughts now.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、証拠物件のキーパー、つまり保管担当を厳密に決められますね
lines.en: Evidence custody is kept under strict protocol, isn't it—with the keeper role clearly assigned?
lines.style: Slight emphasis on 'strict.' Nods with understanding of the seriousness. Slower breath. This one matters. Not questioning, but acknowledging weight.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、エコノミスト誌の犯罪経済特集も参考にされますね
lines.en: They also reference crime economics reporting—from publications like The Economist, I imagine.
lines.style: The list is becoming a rhythm now. Slightly faster pace. A hint of knowing approval in the tone. Small warmth on the example.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 警察、旧ウィルコム端末の通信記録も照会されますね
lines.en: And they can access communication records from older devices too—even old WILLCOM phones.
lines.style: Quieter, more intimate. Leaning in slightly. The final item, delivered with a touch of surprise or newfound respect. Breath trails off a little.
